mostWorthwhile.text: Applying the paid rota was most worthwhile: it turned the care objection into a concrete, revisable arrangement without pretending that costs were settled.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial charter combination was the least engaging because its outcome was fairly predictable from the only offered option, though the distinction between ownership and usable rights was useful.

surprise.text: The final arrangement included an elected care group to fund substitutes and fill gaps, while leaving staffing and costs disputed.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though each decision offered only one combination, so there was little opportunity to explore alternatives.

continue.text: I would continue: the chapter connected autonomy to practical care obligations, and I would be interested in seeing similarly concrete tensions examined elsewhere.
